own_solution.law: Shallow-water wave speed c = sqrt(g h) with h linear in x; t = integral dx/sqrt(g h) = 2L/(sqrt(g)(sqrt(h1)+sqrt(h2))).
assumptions: depth varies linearly with horizontal distance
local shallow-water speed sqrt(g h) applies (wavelength >> depth)

TA114.regime: shallow-water regime: wavelength much greater than depth (roughly lambda > 20 h, i.e. > 4 km for h = 200 m); 170 km is well inside

T5E18.regime: shallow-water regime: wavelength much greater than depth; 170 km >> 200 m

defect_reasons.other: The R sentences say dredging adds 33 m 'at the landward end' without saying the slope stays uniform from 200 m to 93 m; a local hole at the end would leave the time essentially unchanged, though the base's 'slopes uniformly' supports the uniform reading.

notes: Base: sqrt(200)+sqrt(60) = 21.8881; times sqrt(9.8) = 68.5206; t = 120000/68.5206 = 1751.3 s. With landward depth 93 m (uniform slope 200 -> 93 m): sqrt(200)+sqrt(93) = 23.7858; times 3.13050 = 74.4613; t = 1611.6 s. T8491 (dredged before the tsunami arrived) leaves the deepened state in place, so it is R. TEB36/TF161 ('for an earlier survey only') are D, though the phrase is somewhat artificial. Harbour sentences D. Wavelength sentences are K (shallow-water regime). Paired sentences all state 33 m or 170 km consistently; TF161 and T6BFE use 'a little' with no number.
